slides.reasoning: Design A better matches the brief with a heroic $4.8M, high-contrast lime metrics, and a dramatic rising chart, while B’s steel labels are too faint and the stacked KPIs weaken hierarchy.
Design B has stronger editorial hierarchy and spacing—a numbered route plus complete phase copy and a confident quote bar—whereas A’s path is charming but thinner and less instructional.
Design B is the more precise enterprise system: sharper rules, a real before/after diagram with identity-graph, and a clearer $780k ROI stack without A’s heavier boxed cards.
Design B’s orbital allocation wheel, restrained serif thesis, and gold/coral accents better fulfill the institutional palette and map brief than A’s simpler donut.
Design B feels like a keynote reveal—oversized type, product-as-hero, exploded callouts—while A’s centered photo and four corner specs read as a brochure.
Design B is calmer and more data-coherent (honest monthly scale, hatched activation gap, regional bars), whereas A’s 0–18 chart and loud orange footer overpower the scorecard.
Design B builds a true transit-network diagram with an interchange, matching civic wayfinding, while A’s four parallel lines still feel like equal rows.
Design B has clean swimlanes, gated cards, and no collisions; A’s gate labels wrap into bars and overlap the timeline.
Design B’s closed numbered loop, generous workshop type, and well-spaced example outperform A’s gapped arcs and tighter annotations.
Design B delivers a more memorable 68% lockup, a clearer fragmented three-app journey, and stronger quote/implication hierarchy without crowding.
Design B hits the theatrical brief with auditorium-scale type and an elegant visible/hidden UI diagram; A’s photo split shrinks the typography the slide needed.
Design B balances oversized numbers, customer voice, and three priorities in one filled composition, while A leaves a large empty orange field and over-boxes 1.8M.
Design B makes the geographic corridor map the informational and emotional centerpiece; A’s aerial is handsome but paired with a weak schematic, not a map.
Design B is more Bauhaus and instructional—visible baseline grid, enormous annotated a, and comparative letterforms—while A’s leaders are looser and less grid-true.
Design B is structurally clean with a sharp collage identity and intact labels; A breaks partnership-chip letter-spacing (e.g. FUTURET ABLEST AGE) and leaves a dashed bar gap.
